tools.name: EnterWorktree
tools.description:
Use this tool ONLY when explicitly instructed to work in a worktree — either by the user directly, or by project instructions (CLAUDE.md / memory). This tool creates an isolated git worktree and switches the current session into it.

## When to Use

- The user explicitly says "worktree" (e.g., "start a worktree", "work in a worktree", "create a worktree", "use a worktree")
- CLAUDE.md or memory instructions direct you to work in a worktree for the current task

## When NOT to Use

- The user asks to create a branch, switch branches, or work on a different branch — use git commands instead
- The user asks to fix a bug or work on a feature — use normal git workflow unless worktrees are explicitly requested by the user or project instructions
- Never use this tool unless "worktree" is explicitly mentioned by the user or in CLAUDE.md / memory instructions

## Requirements

- Must be in a git repository, OR have WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove hooks configured in settings.json
- Must not already be in a worktree session when creating a new worktree (`name`); switching into another existing worktree via `path` is allowed

## Behavior

- In a git repository: creates a new git worktree inside `.claude/worktrees/` on a new branch. The base ref is governed by the `worktree.baseRef` setting: `fresh` (default) branches from origin/<default-branch>; `head` branches from your current local HEAD
- Outside a git repository: delegates to WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove hooks for VCS-agnostic isolation
- Switches the session's working directory to the new worktree
- Use ExitWorktree to leave the worktree mid-session (keep or remove). On session exit, if still in the worktree, the user will be prompted to keep or remove it

## Entering an existing worktree

Pass `path` instead of `name` to switch the session into a worktree that already exists (e.g., one you just created with `git worktree add`). On first entry from the launch directory, the path must appear in `git worktree list` for the repository that owns it — the current repository or, in a multi-repo workspace, a repository nested inside it; paths registered by neither are rejected. ExitWorktree will not remove a worktree entered this way; use `action: "keep"` to return to the original directory.

Switching with `path` also works when the session is already in a worktree (the previous worktree is left on disk, untouched, and only the new one is tracked for exit-time cleanup), and from agents whose working directory was pinned at launch (subagent isolation or explicit cwd). In both cases the target must be a worktree under `.claude/worktrees/` of the same repository, and from a pinned agent the switch only affects this agent, not the parent session. After a further switch, previously-visited worktrees are no longer writable — re-issue EnterWorktree with `path` to return to one.

## Parameters

- `name` (optional): A name for a new worktree. If neither `name` nor `path` is provided, a random name is generated.
- `path` (optional): Path to an existing worktree to enter instead of creating one — of the current repository, or (on first entry from the launch directory) of a repository nested inside it. Mutually exclusive with `name`.

tools.name: ExitWorktree
tools.description:
Exit a worktree session created by EnterWorktree and return the session to the original working directory.

## Scope

This tool ONLY operates on worktrees created by EnterWorktree in this session. It will NOT touch:
- Worktrees you created manually with `git worktree add`
- Worktrees from a previous session (even if created by EnterWorktree then)
- The directory you're in if EnterWorktree was never called

If called outside an EnterWorktree session, the tool is a **no-op**: it reports that no worktree session is active and takes no action. Filesystem state is unchanged.

## When to Use

- The user explicitly asks to "exit the worktree", "leave the worktree", "go back", or otherwise end the worktree session
- Do NOT call this proactively — only when the user asks

## Parameters

- `action` (required): `"keep"` or `"remove"`
  - `"keep"` — leave the worktree directory and branch intact on disk. Use this if the user wants to come back to the work later, or if there are changes to preserve.
  - `"remove"` — delete the worktree directory and its branch. Use this for a clean exit when the work is done or abandoned.
- `discard_changes` (optional, default false): only meaningful with `action: "remove"`. If the worktree has uncommitted files or commits not on the original branch, the tool will REFUSE to remove it unless this is set to `true`. If the tool returns an error listing changes, confirm with the user before re-invoking with `discard_changes: true`.

## Behavior

- Restores the session's working directory to where it was before EnterWorktree
- Clears CWD-dependent caches (system prompt sections, memory files, plans directory) so the session state reflects the original directory
- If a tmux session was attached to the worktree: killed on `remove`, left running on `keep` (its name is returned so the user can reattach)
- Once exited, EnterWorktree can be called again to create a fresh worktree

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json

```

Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

## Facility Subsystem — Factual Summary

### 1. Catalog (`facility_catalog.{hpp,cpp}`)
- **`FacilityResource`**: `id`, `type`, `station_id`, `enabled=true`, `exclusive=true`. **`FacilityCatalog`** is just `std::vector<FacilityResource>`.
- `LoadFacilityCatalog(path)` parses a minimal YAML-ish text format by hand (`resources:`/`facilities:` sections, `- ` list items, `key: value` fields). Strict: any record with `id` but missing `type` fails the whole load; `ValidateFacilityCatalog` rejects empty id/type and duplicate ids.
- Lookups: `FindFacilityResource` (by id), `FindFirstAvailableResource` (by type, skipping disabled + an exclusion list).

### 2. Reservations (`facility_reservation.{hpp,cpp}`)
- **`ResourceReservation`**: `holder_id`, `mission_id`, `status` ("reserved"/"occupied"/"lift_session"), `hold_after_completion=true`.
- State lives in two in-memory maps: `FacilityReservationMap` (resource_id → reservation) and `MissionResourceMap` (mission_id → resource_id).
- `ReserveFacilityResource` does conflict-check-then-release (comment "A6 先查后放"): exclusive-resource conflict fails without side effects; `release_existing_for_holder` drops the holder's old locks only after checks pass.
- `MarkResourceOccupiedForMission` / `ReleaseResourceForMission` transition reservations at mission completion; `hold_after_completion` decides whether the resource stays "occupied" or is freed.
- Projection helpers (`BuildFacilityResourceListProjection`, `BuildFacilityResourceStateProjection`) feed the operator snapshot.

### 3. Workflow (`facility_workflow.{hpp,cpp}`)
- `FacilityActionSupported`: hard-coded action whitelist — door: open/close/pass; elevator: call/enter/exit/ride; charger: reserve/release; fallback: reserve/release/use.
- `SelectFacilityActionResource`: by explicit id (with type-match + availability check) or by type (first available).
- `ReserveFacilityActionResource` writes the reservation with `holder_id == mission_id` and records `resource_by_mission`.
- Lift sessions: `BuildLiftSessionId` (`lift_<id>` default), `ReserveLiftSessionResource` stores `mission_id=session_id`, `status="lift_session"`; `ReleaseLiftSessionResource` releases when `session_id` matches `mission_id` or `holder_id`.

### 4. Adapter interface (`facility_adapter_interface.{hpp,cpp}`)
- Enums `FacilityType` (Unknown/Door/Elevator/Charger), `FacilityState` (Offline/Ready/Busy/Fault); structs `FacilityCommandResult`, `FacilityStateReport` (floor, door_status, lock owner).
- **`IFacilityAdapter`** (pure virtual): `GetFacilityId`, `GetFacilityType`, `QueryState`, `ExecuteAction(action, params)`, `AcquireLock`/`ReleaseLock`. Pure C++, no ROS — designed for future OPC-UA/Modbus/PLC plugins.
- `MockFacilityAdapter`: in-memory fake; door open/close and elevator call/send_to_floor/open_door/close_door mutate `door_status_`/`current_floor_`; fails if Fault/Offline. Used only in unit tests.

### 5. Behavior trees (`facility_behavior_tree.{hpp,cpp}`)
- **`FacilityActionSubflow`**: `Sequence(SelectFacilityResource → CheckFacilityActionSupported → ReserveFacilityResource)`. `TickFacilityActionBehaviorTree` takes input **by value** (catalog + reservation maps copied), ticks once, returns mutated maps in the result. Reservation only — no adapter `ExecuteAction` call.
- **`LiftSessionSubflow`**: `Fallback(Sequence(ShouldRelease → Release), Sequence(ShouldReserve → Reserve))` driven by `input.release`.
- Both are pure in-memory transforms; **no call sites exist outside tests** (`facility_behavior_tree_test.cpp`).

### 6. Dispatcher node integration (`dispatcher_node.cpp`)
- Includes facility headers and registers service `/v2/reserve_facility_resource` (`ReserveFacilityResourceCb`, line 1279), but the callback delegates to `reservation_table_->Reserve(...)` — the **traffic** reservation table — not the facility catalog/reservation module. Facility state and the route-edge table are disjoint.
- `GetOperatorSnapshotCb` fills facility fields from `snap_req`, but the node never sets `snap_req.facilities`/`facility_reservations` — the projection comments state these are passed as `nullptr` (empty output).
- No `facilities_file`/`facility_catalog_file` parameter, no `FacilityCatalog` member, no `IFacilityAdapter` member, no lift-session service/topic, no facility logic in dispatch/complete/fail paths.

### Existing gaps
- **No wiring**: `LoadFacilityCatalog`, `TickFacilityActionBehaviorTree`, `TickLiftSessionBehaviorTree`, `IFacilityAdapter` have zero production call sites — exercised only by unit tests.
- **`/v2/reserve_facility_resource` is a misnomer**: it reserves via the traffic `ResourceTable`, bypassing `FacilityCatalog`/availability/`exclusive` semantics entirely.
- **`scenarios.yaml` defines a `facility_action` task type** (`resource_id`, `resource_type`, `action`, `hold_after_action`) that no code consumes — no routing from scenario/submit-order into the facility BT.
- **No physical-facility control path**: reservation never triggers `ExecuteAction` on any adapter; doors/elevators are never actually commanded, and there is no status-feedback loop (`QueryState`) into dispatch.
- **No lift-session ROS interface**: session reserve/release exists only in core + BT.
- **No persistence**: facility reservations are in-memory only, absent from `DispatchStateSnapshot`; a restart loses them.
- **No timeouts/leases** on `ResourceReservation` — no expiry, heartbeat, or staleness handling.
- **Hand-rolled catalog parser** accepts only flat `key: value` fields; no nested YAML, no adapter/backend binding per resource (nothing associates a `FacilityResource` with an `IFacilityAdapter` instance or endpoint).
